A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Conformal Thinking by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including the new appendix in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on risk calibration and reasoning efficiency across four models, plus validation-size and distribution-shift ablations in Figures 4–9.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix D, including accuracy–token comparisons and risk-control ablations.

M1.justification: V1's slope-controlled sigmoid centered at half the token budget becomes a more general threshold with tunable slope, horizontal shift, and lower asymptote in v2 Section 4.3. Upper-threshold scaling already existed in v1. The stopping framework, four losses, and sequential calibration remain, making this a localized method extension.

E1.justification: Both versions use AIME, DeepScaleR, GPQA-Diamond, and MathVision, retaining the same solvability mixtures and length/domain-shift scenarios. Newly discussed applications and cited benchmarks are not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Confidence, EAT, probes where available, token-count stopping, and signal selection; Naive versus UCB calibration; and upper-only, lower-only, combined, and token-budget policies. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains the models, dataset sizes, chunk-based signal extraction, 50-example calibration sets, and risk sweep in increments of 0.01. The ablation still uses 800 test examples and validation sizes of 8, 16, and 40. No revised experimental settings are established for the generalized threshold.

E4.justification: The solvability-mixture analysis and validation-size, reasoning-length-shift, and dataset-shift ablations are unchanged in Figures 6–9. V1 Appendix C becomes v2 Appendix D. The new Appendix C is a mathematical derivation, not an additional empirical robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over 40 random validation–test splits in Figure 4. Appendix B retains the same Hoeffding correction and fixed-candidate/multiple-comparison caveat. V2's formal guarantee statement does not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Figures 1–9 retain identical plotted data, including risk curves, accuracy–token tradeoffs, exit breakdowns, and ablation results. The accompanying empirical findings are retained; the new appendix contains symbolic reasoning rather than new experimental outcomes.

T1.justification: V2 adds joint and separate risk formulations, an explicit high-probability statement for selected hyperparameters, and a monotonicity assumption in Sections 4.1 and 4.4. New Appendix C derives how differential abstention changes retained-answer error rates. Together these substantially expand the formal treatment, although the basic losses and Appendix B's fixed-candidate bound remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain risk-calibrated reasoning termination, a dynamic lower threshold for insufficient progress, and efficiency gains from combining thresholds and selecting signals. The new conclusion reiterates these claims without reporting stronger empirical achievements.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly identifies assumed risk monotonicity and restriction to scientific/mathematical tasks as limitations. It sharpens v1's existing warning about interacting thresholds through an abstention-rate condition and additional distribution-shift discussion. Interpretations of the empirical results remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract, absent from v1. Section 5.1's generation details and Appendix A's signal-extraction and probe-training specifications remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3 substantially expands positioning against shorter-chain selection/decoding and risk-controlled early-exit networks, adding relevant conformal-risk references. It also acknowledges Thought Calibration's ability to terminate unsolvable instances and refines the distinction from that work. Renamed Wei and Zeng references correspond to existing cited works.

P1.justification: The background and method exposition are extensively rewritten and reorganized around the two-threshold policy, losses, dynamic threshold, and calibration. V2 adds a conclusion/limitations/future-work section and a derivation appendix. The contribution list also introduces an apparent wording error, saying stopping occurs when confidence increases sufficiently, contrary to Section 4.3.

P2.justification: The same nine figures are retained without changed plots or legends. Figure 3 and Algorithm 1 move columns, other figures move with text reflow, and Figures 8–9 now share the final appendix page. Caption equation references and publication formatting are updated.

improvement.justification: V2 improves clarity and transparency through reorganized method exposition, fuller research positioning, explicit assumptions and applicability limitations, and a code link. These gains are limited: Appendix B's calibration caveat remains unresolved, and the contribution list introduces a reversed stopping-condition sentence. The unchanged empirical evidence supports a modest overall improvement.
